risks.risk: The photo may be panels, but the seller’s claims are about a battery; the actual item you’d receive could be different (panels vs battery vs full system).
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the exact item(s) being sold laid out: battery label/terminal area, inverter/charge controller (if included), and the panel nameplate.
risks.if_unproven: Price as solar panels only (no battery/inverter included) and at worst-case for unknown panel wattage.

risks.risk: Panel wattage/model and quality (e.g., mono vs poly, efficiency class) are not readable, so the total system value is unknown.
risks.proof: Request a close-up photo of the panel label/nameplate showing brand, model, and rated wattage (W).
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic/unknown-rated solar panels (lowest plausible wattage) with no performance guarantee.

risks.risk: Quantity is unclear (how many panels total). Photo 0 shows at least two, but not the full count.
risks.proof: Request a photo showing the full set with a count (or a wide shot including all panels in the frame).
risks.if_unproven: Price for the minimum visible quantity (as seen) until total count is confirmed.

risks.risk: Condition/age and any damage (cracks, delamination, water ingress) can’t be assessed from this single image.
risks.proof: Request close-up photos of panel corners/edges and the glass surface (including any visible defects).
risks.if_unproven: Price as used/possibly imperfect condition (worst-case) until defect-free condition is shown.

proof_requests: Close-up of the panel nameplate/label (brand, model, rated wattage W, serial if available).
A wide shot showing the full number of panels included.
Photos of the battery (if included): brand/model label, capacity (Ah/Wh), date/production sticker, and terminal condition.
If a battery is claimed: a short video test showing voltage under load and/or a charge/discharge test result (to support the “8 hours” claim).
Photos of any inverter/charge controller included (front label/model).
